findings.title: Date recovery blocks Ctrl+C while its synchronous search runs
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Availability and private-screen cleanup failure; no incorrect recovered wallet or secret exfiltration was demonstrated.
reproduction: Run security-cancellation.py on Linux with Node 26.10.0, fresh dist and the canonical protection flags. The real CLI is attached to a pseudo-terminal.
Use public zero-entropy BIP39 words as the shifted input; seedshift mode, English format, date 01-01-????, public synthetic master fingerprint deadbeef, max-candidates 10000 and progress-every 1.
Send SIGINT after the first Checked N/9999 progress count. The probe enforces a 0.75-second observation window and kills its own process group before three seconds total.
findings.expected: SIGINT should promptly invoke the private-screen interrupt handler, clear and leave the alternate screen, and end with 130.
findings.observed: On the unsandboxed host, 355 further candidates were computed after SIGINT; no leave-alternate-screen sequence appeared. The process required the probe SIGKILL guard, returning -9 after 1.735 seconds overall. The sandbox PTY run independently showed 415 further candidates and the same behavior.
findings.rootCause: The complete dateRecoveryCandidates loop, wallet evidence PBKDF2 checks and progress output run synchronously without yielding to the event loop. The private-screen SIGINT handler cannot execute until that work returns.
findings.impact: A supported search that can take hours cannot be stopped promptly using its normal Ctrl+C path; a force kill bypasses private-screen cleanup. This demonstrates responsiveness and screen cleanup failure, not data exfiltration.
findings.recommendedFix: Yield to the event loop after a bounded amount of date-recovery work, like recover-word already does, so the existing SIGINT handler can run. Keep private-screen cleanup and data ownership in finally scopes.
findings.requiredVerification: Rerun the retained PTY probe expecting CLI exit 130 and an alternate-screen leave sequence without forced kill; confirm unchanged candidate enumeration and recovery results with scoped date tests.

findings.title: Semantically invalid public-key and WIF evidence is reported as a non-match
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Valid evidence comparisons pass. Impact is malformed-evidence diagnostics and unnecessary recovery work; no incorrect positive match or spending-authority compromise was demonstrated.
findings.reproduction: Use matchBitcoinEvidence with the public zero-entropy phrase, location mainnet/account 0/branch 0/index 0, native-segwit profile, and compressed-public-key value 02 followed by 32 ff bytes. Independently packed checksum-valid compressed WIFs for scalar zero and the secp256k1 group order produce the same result. The actual recover-word CLI is also run with eleven abandon words and ?, plus that invalid public key.
findings.expected: Reject the invalid secp256k1 point or scalar as malformed recovery evidence before deriving candidate wallets.
findings.observed: Direct public-key and both WIF comparisons return {matched:false,kind:...}. Actual CLI exits 0, emits 128 non-match rows and says Matched 0 of 128 candidates against the requested compressed public key locally.
findings.impact: Corrupted key evidence can be presented as evidence against all candidates and consume a configured search. No valid recovered wallet can match these invalid mathematical keys. This is input-validation correctness; a missing wallet result is not evidence of financial loss.
findings.recommendedFix: Validate compressed points with the dependency curve validator and WIF scalars against 1 <= k < n before comparison. Keep stable redacted errors and wipe decoded WIF buffers.
findings.requiredVerification: Reject public x >= p and non-curve points, WIF k=0 and k>=n, and preserve valid points/WIF on both networks and all profiles.

findings.title: An empty candidate word place causes an unbounded search
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The CLI parser cannot create an empty place. Demonstrated reachability is the explicitly reusable direct host module with a structurally legal TypeScript readonly number[] value.
findings.reproduction: Construct {kind:"unknown-words",places:[...eleven [0] arrays,[]]}; searchCombinations returns 0. Call searchCandidates(search).next() in a bounded child process.
findings.expected: Reject a search with an empty word place before enumeration, or terminate with zero candidates.
findings.observed: The child synchronously confirms entered:true,combinations:0, then never returns within one second; the harness kills it with SIGKILL/ETIMEDOUT. Static loop increments the empty place counter indefinitely because 0 never equals length-1 (-1).
findings.impact: A host that builds its own WordSearch can block its execution thread on an empty filtered place despite the stated combination limit. This is not reachable through parseUnknownWords, which rejects empty prefixes/choices. No ordinary CLI input hang was demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Validate search kind, supported phrase length, nonempty places and integer indexes at searchCandidates entry; reject before computing work bounds or enumeration.
findings.requiredVerification: An empty place rejects or returns zero promptly; valid prefix/choice searches retain ordering; unknown discriminants, invalid lengths and index values are bounded and rejected.

findings.title: Invalid date-recovery mode silently selects checksum-valid Seedshift
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Supported mode strings work; CLI transformMode validates them. The failure is confined to library or direct-host callers passing an invalid discriminant.
findings.reproduction: Encode the public abandon-times-11/about mnemonic with 23-09-2026; call dateRecoveryCandidates(indexes, [], [parseDatePattern("?3-09-2026")], "seedshift-typo") and consume it. The harness also passes direct, undefined and null.
findings.expected: Reject each unsupported or missing SeedshiftMode instead of choosing a valid transformation.
findings.observed: All four invalid modes yield three checksum-valid candidates, byte-for-byte equal to explicit seedshift mode.
findings.impact: A malformed host configuration silently uses a different decoder. This can produce plausible valid phrases or false-negative wallet evidence during recovery. The CLI is protected by transformMode validation; no correct typed mode failure, secret disclosure or financial loss was demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Validate the mode at the generator boundary or use an exhaustive switch whose default throws a redacted unsupported-mode error.
findings.requiredVerification: All three supported modes retain expected candidates; unknown strings, direct, null and omitted mode throw before decoding.
findings.skepticDisposition: Reduced to low: malformed runtime arguments are required; valid typed and CLI inputs pass.

findings.title: Non-string BIP39 passphrases are silently converted into wallet salts
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The CLI reads passphrases as strings and normal supported strings match independent BIP39 outputs. Failure concerns invalid runtime arguments in the public library API.
findings.reproduction: Call masterFingerprint(publicZeroMnemonic, null), then with 123, false, [], {}. Compare with the documented @scure/bip39 mnemonicToSeedSync boundary and explicit String(argument).
findings.expected: Reject non-string passphrases, matching the documented dependency contract, while undefined continues to mean the optional default empty passphrase.
findings.observed: @scure/bip39 rejects all five inputs. MnemoCode accepts each and exactly matches String(argument): null -> fingerprint 8ea49d40, 123 -> fb6875cd, false -> c0a0b658, [] -> 73c5da0a, {} -> b27a08e4.
findings.impact: A malformed host value can silently select a different BIP39 wallet; an empty array silently selects the no-passphrase wallet. This applies to the shared rootForMnemonic path used by evidence matching. Correct string passphrases pass the independent oracle; no CLI passphrase failure or private-material disclosure was demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Check typeof passphrase === "string" before interpolating the mnemonic salt and preserve existing well-formed Unicode/NFKD rules.
findings.requiredVerification: Null, numbers, booleans, arrays and objects reject. Empty/Unicode string and omitted/undefined default behavior remain correct across all supported lengths.
findings.skepticDisposition: Reduced to low: malformed runtime arguments are required; valid typed and CLI inputs pass.

findings.releaseBlockingReason: A valid quorum still recovers correct entropy; no secret compromise demonstrated. Surplus-member integrity and reliability guidance should be corrected before claiming every supplied share is checked.
findings.title: Complete recovery silently ignores inconsistent surplus members
findings.upstreamCause: sskr 0.12.0 encoding.rs combine_shares retains only the first member_threshold shares per group and stops after group_threshold successfully restored groups.
findings.reproduction: Use vectors.deterministic[0] shares 0 and 1, modify byte 8 of share 2 CBOR and independently recompute CRC32. Supply all three to combineSskrShares and checkShareBackup; also supply [share0, modifiedShare2].
findings.expected: Reject the supplied inconsistent set, or explicitly report which supplied shares were unchecked rather than representing the entire set as valid.
findings.observed: Three-share combine returns original mnemonic, backup check returns restores, but the pair containing altered member rejects. Modified share: ur:sskr/goemjzaeadaockjsrpamsebalrbysbjngeeysnplutlyktgresnd.
findings.impact: A checksum-valid wrong surplus member survives a complete-set recovery/check. The nominal any-2-of-3 redundancy can fail after the valid pair is separated or one correct share is lost. Prerequisite is a structurally valid incorrect surplus share, such as manual alteration plus recalculated CRC or same-identifier collision; ordinary mistyping with invalid CRC still rejects. This is not an authenticity guarantee against arbitrary malicious shares.
findings.recommendedFix: Check all supplied complete members against each group's recovered threshold polynomial, as joint repair already does; account separately for incomplete groups. Alternatively accurately expose ignored shares and constrain reliability claims.
findings.evidence: sskr-defects.log, test inconsistent-surplus-share-must-be-rejected; command exit 1 retains production failures.
findings.requiredVerification: Test altered first and surplus members in different orders, all possible surviving pairs, surplus groups and incomplete groups; preserve successful valid grouped quorums.

findings.releaseBlockingReason: Limited to compatibility layouts; current canonical transport repair passes. Documented existing-backup acceptance should extend consistently to repair.
findings.title: Repair rejects transport layouts accepted by complete-share recovery
findings.reproduction: Encode public deterministic first share transport as untagged full Bytewords, or prefix its CBOR with current tag 40309/legacy tag 309 and independently recompute CRC to create tagged UR. Intact normalizeShare/combine succeed. Replace token 13 with ? and call readRepairableShare/combine; also mix intact legacy Bytewords with a marked canonical second share.
findings.expected: Repair one missing transport unit for every accepted layout, and accept the unchanged legacy member when another share is damaged.
findings.observed: All three marked compatibility layouts yield No valid share fits the marked elements; joint plan yields no-fit, Share 1 is no share. The untouched legacy member likewise causes no-fit when only the other member is marked.
findings.impact: Users restoring supported older backups can be blocked by one unreadable token despite a recoverable CRC system. A fully legible legacy member can block repair of a different member. Canonical current untagged UR and tagged full Bytewords are unaffected.
findings.recommendedFix: Let standardStructures enumerate all tagged/untagged layouts accepted by transport.ts for both standard textual forms. Keep CBOR, metadata, CRC and digest validation unchanged; normalize intact members before constructing repair spaces where appropriate.
findings.evidence: sskr-defects.log, four compatibility checks failed; intact acceptance and no-fit assessments printed for each.
findings.requiredVerification: One-token first/middle/last repair of legacy untagged Bytewords, current/legacy tagged UR and supported long CBOR length layout; joint repair with intact legacy and marked current members in both orders.

findings.title: Menu redraw leaves stale selections when terminal lines wrap
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The defect obscures navigation in narrow terminals; standard-width navigation and direct CLI commands remain usable.
findings.reproduction: Run the normal protected launcher in a 40-row by 40-column pseudo-terminal with NO_COLOR=1 and TERM=xterm. Press Down twice. Capture the actual output and replay its VT cursor/erase controls with terminal wrapping. A 120-column control is run first.
findings.expected: Exactly one visible selection should represent the current choice after a redraw, including when the terminal is narrower than 78 columns.
findings.observed: The 120-column capture has one selection marker. The 40-column capture has three visible selection markers after two Down keys, with old item rows left above the current menu. LINE_WIDTH is fixed at 78 and redrawFrom receives logical line counts, while labels and hints occupy multiple physical rows.
findings.impact: A user in a narrow terminal sees conflicting selected tasks and repeated rows. The probe does not establish incorrect command dispatch or secret leakage.
findings.recommendedFix: Account for the actual terminal column count and wrapped physical rows, or lay out/truncate each row to the current width before counting rows for redraw. Handle terminal resize consistently.
findings.requiredVerification: Repeat the real protected PTY probe at 120, 80, 60 and 40 columns, including arrow navigation, selection, Escape and a resize, and confirm one visible selection with no stale rows.

findings.title: Displayed equivalent command changes shell-sensitive filename arguments
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The active menu executes an argv array safely; this defect affects the command string shown for copying and later use.
findings.reproduction: Call the production typedCommand with ['preview','--pdf','output/a$(printf b).pdf']. Run the returned command in Bash with a harmless mnemocode function that prints its arguments instead of rendering anything.
findings.expected: The 'The same as:' command must preserve the exact filename literal when copied to a supported shell.
findings.observed: typedCommand returns mnemocode preview --pdf "output/a$(printf b).pdf". Bash expands the substitution and passes output/ab.pdf instead of the requested literal filename. Double quotes escape only double-quote characters, leaving dollar signs, backticks and backslashes with shell meaning.
findings.impact: Copying the offered command can change the output destination. The harmless printf probe proves substitution; it does not imply an attacker supplies filenames or that active menu execution evaluates shell text.
findings.recommendedFix: Use a tested shell-quoting routine appropriate to the supported shell and platform, or clearly display an argv representation that is not presented as a copyable equivalent shell command.
findings.requiredVerification: Round-trip synthetic filenames with spaces, dollar signs, literal substitutions, backticks, backslashes, quotes and Unicode through the displayed command in supported shells; confirm arguments match byte for byte and no expansion runs.

findings.title: Executable build failures can remove the previous file or leave mixed artifact generations
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The script fails and the current workflow does not upload/publish on this failed step; no unsafe successful release is demonstrated.
findings.reproduction: Run node --experimental-vm-modules docs/audits/AUD-008-harnesses/devops-build-failure.mjs. The harness evaluates the current production script with mock filesystem/build operations, prepopulates an existing executable/sidecar/checksum, and injects failures at bundling, SEA generation and notice generation.
findings.expected: A failed rebuild preserves the previous usable artifact set and removes its temporary build directory. Stage successful replacements before final publication.
findings.observed: Bundler failure preserves the executable but leaves work. SEA failure occurs after rmSync(executable): the old binary is absent, old sidecar/checksum remain, and work is not removed. Notice generation failure occurs after the new executable is installed: old notices/checksums remain beside the new binary. Corrected harness exits 1 with all three expected baseline assertions and no real writes/builds.
findings.impact: A local rebuild can discard a working executable or leave an executable with obsolete checksum/notices until rerun; build failures also leave temporary work. No real secret data or successful CI publication is implicated.
findings.prerequisites: An existing output artifact set and a subsequent failure at the relevant build phase.
findings.recommendedFix: Build/sign the executable, assemble notices and compute checksums in a temporary sibling staging directory. Complete these steps before replacing final artifacts, with rollback/preservation semantics and unconditional finally cleanup.
findings.requiredVerification: Inject bundler, SEA, signing, notices and checksum/write failures; assert the prior complete artifact set remains identical and temporary work is removed. Then run the documented executable verifier on the supported systems when release-level execution is authorized.
findings.limits: Mocked execution proves the first-party sequencing/failure cleanup, not Node SEA/esbuild/signing correctness or an actual platform failure.

findings.title: Security policy gives conflicting descriptions of CLI permission restrictions
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Documentation ambiguity; the canonical launcher denied the reviewed scopes.
findings.reproduction: Read Security model alongside Secret lifecycle and local boundaries. Compare with the canonical CLI permission observation and its explicitly granted-rights control.
findings.expected: Distinguish the normal CLI's Node permission restrictions from an unisolated library host and from operating-system isolation. State whether deliberate launch grants are trusted.
findings.observed: The first description says the program runs with the starting Node process's file/process/network rights, while the later one says it always denies network/workers/addons. Normal relaunch denies them, but explicitly pre-granted rights survive. The library-host warning itself remains correct.
findings.impact: Readers receive inconsistent descriptions of what the launcher enforces. No default network transmission or malicious-code isolation guarantee is established.
findings.recommendedFix: Describe the normal CLI restriction and library-host responsibilities separately, retain the trusted offline-computer requirement, and qualify intentional permission overrides unless the launcher explicitly drops them.
findings.requiredVerification: Check the revised wording against normal-launch and intentionally pre-granted scope probes. Do not imply an OS sandbox or remove the offline warning.

informationalNotes.title: Short repair cancellation and build cleanup

The SSKR verification script's direct process.exit bypasses finally on mismatch. These remain source-reviewed cleanup opportunities, not separately reproduced compromise claims.

skepticDispositions.reason: Real supported CLI search and documented private-screen interrupt promise; synchronous source loop confirms PTY evidence.
CLI reachable. Independent OpenSSL rejects the same curve point; comparator silently returns non-match. WIF scalar range follows the same missing semantic validation.

An empty readonly array is structurally valid; the reusable direct module hangs. It is not re-exported from the stable root facade and CLI parsing prevents this shape; those limits must remain explicit.
Only invalid runtime discriminants violate the TypeScript contract; correct modes and CLI paths pass. Runtime rejection is useful, but no normal-mode failure is demonstrated.
Native PBKDF2 interpolation differs from the previous dependency boundary. Malformed non-string host values are needed; CLI and valid string inputs remain correct.

Root independently altered another payload byte: the full set passes and the pair with that member fails. A valid quorum really does restore; the unsupported claim is that surplus backup members have thereby been validated. CRC-valid altered content is a prerequisite; ordinary CRC-detected typos are not silently accepted.

Root confirmed an intact accepted legacy Bytewords member causes no-fit when another canonical member is marked. Accepted transport/repair contracts diverge. Legacy compatibility can be narrowed explicitly instead of mandated universally.
Actual PTY output wraps; source redraw counts logical rows. Minimal VT replay is evidence with an explicit rendering limitation, not a screenshot.
Double quotes permit shell expansion. Active menu execution passes an argv array safely; no attacker-controlled filename injection is alleged.
Exact-source mocked failure proves ordering and cleanup defects. Failed workflow steps do not publish; no actual SEA failure or fresh rebuild was run.
README and heirs explicitly distinguish a valid checksum from correct dates. An immediate runtime reminder would help but no checksum guarantee or arithmetic defect is inferred.
Requires deliberate trusted caller rights. Default launcher denies the scopes; no exfiltration.
Missing wipes demonstrated under retained references; no production GC lifetime or cross-process memory disclosure established. Tighten ownership without claiming guaranteed JS erasure.
Missing documents matter if package archives become a supported distribution; current private/repository distribution retains them.
